videos.title: Why the Tiger Sees Six Times Better in the Dark #Shorts

comments.author: @pierred3632
comments.text: They should make cataract lenses for old people like these !
comments.replyText: Nature's engineering is way ahead of us! The tapetum lucidum is basically a biological mirror that doubles light input. Researchers are actually studying this structure for next-gen night vision tech. Appreciate you watching and dropping a comment!

clipCandidates.why: Relatable connection: the glowing eye shine in cat photos at night is the tapetum reflecting flash — connects everyday experience to biology
clipCandidates.hookRewrite: Why cat eyes glow in photos and yours don't

clipCandidates.why: Powerful closer with vertical slit pupil detail — tiger doesn't just survive the dark, it owns it
clipCandidates.hookRewrite: When the jungle goes dark this predator sees everything

videos.title: Why the Peacock Glows Without Pigment #Shorts

clipCandidates.momentLabel: Grind to dust and color vanishes
clipCandidates.why: Most mind-blowing moment: grinding a peacock feather to dust makes the color disappear — the pigment was never there, only the architecture of light
clipCandidates.hookRewrite: Grind this feather to dust and the color completely vanishes

clipCandidates.why: Core science: millions of microscopic ridges interfere with light waves, canceling some and amplifying others — same physics as soap bubbles
clipCandidates.hookRewrite: These colors exist without any pigment at all

clipCandidates.hookRewrite: This bird turned poison water into an all-you-can-eat buffet
